info.title: Patrolli API
info.description: RESTful API for Patrolli monitoring system

post.description:
Updates a user's password after verifying their current credentials.
Only for the caller's own password; changing another user's password is
`PATCH /api/v1/users/{user_id}`.

403.description: Account has no password or is disabled

post.description: Authenticates a user with username and password and returns a token pair.

Revokes the refresh token. Any access token already issued stays valid until
it expires, which is why its lifetime is short.

Exchanges a refresh token for a new access token. The refresh token itself is
returned unchanged and stays valid until it expires; rotation is not implemented.

get.description: Returns all hosts from the database

post.description: Creates a new host in the database

put.description: Updates an existing host in the database and cache

delete.description: Deletes a host from the database and cache

get.description: Returns all items from the database

parameters.name: template_ids
parameters.description: Return items that from specified template IDs. This includes items that are defined in the templates, as well as items that are used by hosts that use the templates.

parameters.name: host_ids
parameters.description: Return items that are used by the specified host IDs. This includes items from templates used by the hosts, as well as items directly defined on the hosts.

parameters.name: exclusivity
parameters.description:
If specified, include items based on their exclusivity:
- `host`: include items that are directly defined on hosts
- `template`: include items that are defined in templates but not used by any hosts
- `template_on_host`: include items that are defined in templates and used by hosts

If multiple exclusivity options are specified, items that match any of the specified exclusivity will be included. If no exclusivity is specified, items of all exclusivity will be included.

parameters.name: endpoint_ids
parameters.description: If specified, only return items that are associated with the specified endpoint IDs

parameters.name: listener_ids
parameters.description: If specified, only return items that are associated with the specified listener IDs

parameters.name: processor_id
parameters.description: If specified, only return items that outputs to the specified processor ID

parameters.name: types
parameters.description: If specified, only return items that are of the specified types

parameters.name: collect_item_stats
parameters.description: If `true``, try to collect ItemStats from peers in cluster.

post.summary: Create an item for a host
Create an item for a template

put.description:
Deprecated: use PUT /items/{item_id}/host, PUT /items/{item_id}/template or
PUT /items/{item_id}/applied-template instead.

put.summary: Update an applied template item by ID
put.description:
Only accepts items on a host that are derived from a template item. name,
schedule, timeout_ms and config are optional: leave them null to keep
inheriting the template item's value, or set them to override it. A config
override cannot change the item type.

400.description: Item is not an applied template item

put.summary: Update a host item by ID
put.description:
Only accepts items that belong directly to a host, i.e. items that are not
template items and not derived from a template item.

400.description: Item is not a host item

put.summary: Update a template item by ID
put.description:
Only accepts items that belong to a template, they have no listener or
endpoint association. An item linked from another template inherits name,
schedule, timeout_ms and config: leave them null to keep inheriting, or set
them to override. On a template item that is not linked to a template they
are mandatory. A config cannot change the item type, not even on a template
item that is not linked to a template, since the items derived from it keep
their own type.

400.description: Item is not a template item

get.description: Returns information about every node registered in the cluster
Returns public pipelines and the caller's private ones.

post.description: The caller becomes the owner. The pipeline starts with one empty canvas.

404.description: Pipeline not found or not visible to the caller

put.description:
Replaces the name, visibility, status and the host and sink subsets.
Disabling a pipeline stops what its sources receive from going further,
without sending it anywhere else.

403.description: Only the owner can change the visibility

404.description: Pipeline not found or not visible to the caller

409.description: The pipeline was saved after the caller read it, or a dropped host or sink is still used; `error.data` is a PipelineSubsetInUse

delete.description:
Only the owner can delete a pipeline. A pipeline whose owner was deleted
can be deleted by anyone.

404.description: Pipeline not found or not visible to the caller

get.summary: Get the graph of a canvas
get.description:
Returns the structure of the canvas. Sources and processor groups carry a
summary of their content; the full content is read per node.

404.description: Pipeline or canvas not found, or pipeline not visible to the caller

put.summary: Save the graph of a canvas
put.description:
Saves the structure only: nodes with their names and positions, and
relations. A new node starts empty and its content is saved per node. A
node left out of the graph is deleted with its content.

404.description: Pipeline or canvas not found, or pipeline not visible to the caller

409.description: The canvas was saved after the caller read it

get.summary: Get the content of a node
get.description:
A source holds items, read one page at a time. A processor group holds
its processors with their config. A sink node shows its sink.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Source nodes only: keep items whose name contains this, ignoring case.

404.description: Pipeline, canvas or node not found, or pipeline not visible to the caller

put.summary: Save the content of a node
put.description:
A source takes items to add and to remove. A processor group takes its
whole processor list in execution order: new ids are created, missing ids
are deleted. A sink node takes a sink of the pipeline, or null to empty it.

200.description: Saved node, a source with its first page of items

404.description: Pipeline, canvas or node not found, or pipeline not visible to the caller

409.description: The node was saved after the caller read it

get.summary: Get the full graph of all resources in the system.
get.description:
Returns all hosts, items, listeners, processors, and sinks as nodes,
with edges representing their relationships.

post.summary: Apply multiple templates to multiple hosts
post.description:
Apply a set of templates to a set of hosts. All specified hosts must not
have any existing connection (direct or through template inheritance) to
any of the specified templates. If any host already has a connection to
any template, the operation is rejected and no changes are made.

400.description: No host IDs or template IDs provided

404.description: One or more hosts/templates not found

409.description: One or more hosts already have a connection to a template

put.summary: Link a template to another template

404.description: Template not found/Template destination not found

post.summary: Unapply multiple pair of host_id and template_id
post.description:
Removing a template from a host will either delete the items that were created
from the template, or resolve their inherited fields and keep them as local items.

404.description: Host not found / Template not found / Template not applied to host

put.summary: Unlink a template from another template

404.description: Template not found / Template destination not found / Link not found

patch.description:
Only the fields present in the body are changed. This is also where another
user's password is changed, without their current password. It is meant for
admins and will be protected by RBAC in the future.

post.description:
The next SSO login that matches the username links again, so this also fixes a
user whose identity provider account was recreated. `allow_sso` is not changed.

get.description: Returns the health status of the API server, database connection, and cache

AttributeCollect.description:
Collect complete rows from incoming attributes into mutable lookup tables.

Each rule produces one row per source parent and upserts it under the
target table's configured key. An existing row is replaced in full and its
TTL refreshed, never merged. TTL, capacity and key definitions belong to the
lookup table.

Missing inputs, null keys or bounds and failed conversions skip the whole
candidate row and count an error; an explicit null non-key value is stored
as null, and capacity rejections are counted separately. Telemetry always
passes through unchanged.

collections.description:
Collection rules; must not be empty. All read incoming attributes and
may target the same lookup table. A repeated key replaces the whole row
in write order, which concurrent writers do not order by event time.

oneOf.description:
Record-selection predicate over incoming attributes, evaluated once for
all rules and ANDed with each rule's own `when`. Omitted means every
record is eligible. A predicate error skips all collection without
dropping telemetry.

For a resource or scope rule every predicate leaf must reference that
rule's source table, so selection is uniform for its shared parent; a
record rule may reference any table. Selection is per record.

One entry of `columns`: `null` for a pivoted binding with every option
defaulted, otherwise an [`AttributeCollectInput`].

AttributeCollectCast.description:
Supported column conversions. Unlike lookup probe casts, this includes
doubles because collection also supplies non-key value columns.

AttributeCollectInput.description:
One column's source: an exact attribute key, or — without `key` and with a
`pivot` on the rule — the field of an array element selected by name.

oneOf.description:
Explicit conversion before writing. Without a cast the input must
already match the column's declared type. A conversion failure skips the
whole candidate row; there is no implicit stringification.

`double` is allowed for a value column, never a hash or partition key.
A range bound must use `integer` or `ip`, matching the table's range.

An `ip` column always needs `cast: ip`, bound or not, because the input
arrives as a string and would otherwise fail the column's type check and
skip the row. A missing or contradicting cast is rejected when the table
resolves.

key.description:
Dotted attribute key, matched byte for byte. A flattened array element
is addressed by its literal index, such as `interfaces.0.ifIndex`; no
segment carries a special meaning. Column inputs align by parent ID,
never by Arrow row position; the stored key comes from the configured
key-column values.

Omitted, the binding is pivoted and the rule must set `pivot`.

name.description:
Pivoted bindings only: the normalized element name to bind when it
differs from the lookup-table column name, so a column `description`
can be fed by the object `ifDescr`.

oneOf.description:
Only with `key`. Defaults to the rule's source table. A record rule may
also read a resource attribute through the record's resource ID. No
other cross-table read is supported.

value.description:
Pivoted bindings only: the element field supplying the cell instead of
`pivot.value`, for instance `value` to store the raw SNMP value where
the default is the MIB-formatted one.

AttributeCollectPivot.description:
Turn the elements of one flattened array into named columns.

OTAP flattens an array of maps into `<array>.<n>.<field>` attributes, where
`<n>` is the element's position. Position is not a stable identity — the SNMP
walk, for instance, appends values in completion order and skips absent
ones — so a pivoted column is found by the value of one sibling field (the
`name`) and read from another (the `value`). With `array: snmp.data`,
`name: oid_name`, `value: value_formatted` and the `snmp_object` format, the
element `snmp.data.3.oid_name = "IF-MIB::ifDescr.33"` supplies column
`ifDescr` from `snmp.data.3.value_formatted`.

Every pivoted column of a rule is looked up in the same array. Two elements
of one record that normalize to the same name resolve to the highest `<n>`.

array.description:
Dotted key of the flattened array, such as `snmp.data`; its elements are
the attributes `<array>.<n>.<field>` for a nonnegative decimal `<n>`.

name.description:
Element field whose string value names the column, such as `oid_name`.
An element whose name field is missing, not a string, or normalizes to
nothing binds no column.

oneOf.description:
How a raw name becomes the name matched against the columns. Omitted
uses the raw name verbatim.

value.description:
Element field supplying the cell unless the binding overrides it with
its own `value`, such as `value_formatted`.

AttributeCollectRule.description: One mutable lookup table and the source attributes that populate its rows.

columns.description:
Lookup-table column name -> source binding. Must bind every declared
column exactly once, hash keys and range partition/start/end columns
included; an unknown column is rejected when the table resolves. YAML
map order determines neither schema nor composite-key order.

A binding with a `key` reads that exact attribute. A `null` binding, or
one without `key`, is *pivoted*: it reads the `pivot.value` field of the
array element whose normalized name equals the column name (or the
binding's `name`), and requires `pivot` on the rule.

A hash key is taken from the resulting row. In a range table the bound
columns supply the interval, whose type and inclusive ends the table
defines; bounds are consumed by the index, not stored as readable
values. There is no match block and no per-processor key, TTL or
capacity setting.

A missing input or failed cast skips the whole candidate row, leaving
any existing row untouched. No partial updates, no fallback values.

lookup_table.description:
UUID of a configured lookup table whose source is `processor` (mutable);
file-backed tables are not writable. Names are not unique identifiers.

oneOf.description:
Bind columns to the elements of one flattened array by a naming field
rather than by element position. Required by, and only useful with,
bindings in `columns` that have no `key`. Elements are read from the
rule's source table.

table.description:
Source attribute table and default location of column inputs. `record`
means log, span or metric attributes, excluding data-point attributes.
A rule produces one row per eligible parent.

oneOf.description:
Further record-selection predicate, ANDed with the top-level `when`.
Omitted adds no restriction. A predicate error skips only this rule.

A record rule may reference record, resource or scope attributes; a
resource or scope rule only its own table, inherited guard included.
Selection is over whole records.

AttributeLookup.description:
Enrich attributes with independent lookups, applying their writes together.

Every rule reads the incoming attributes: another rule's outputs are not
visible as inputs. Each parent matches at most one lookup row, whose
selected columns supply scalar output attributes.

Missing inputs, failed casts, lookup misses and null result cells leave the
destination unchanged; invalid inputs are counted separately from misses.
Defaults and fallback expressions are not supported.

lookups.description:
Independent enrichment rules; must not be empty. Destination keys must
not overlap within an attribute table, so rule order carries no
precedence.

overwrite.description:
Replace existing destination values. Defaults to insert-only: a key
already present for the destination parent, even with a null value, is
left unchanged. Applies to every rule.

oneOf.description:
Record-selection predicate over incoming attributes, evaluated once for
all rules and ANDed with each rule's own `when`. Omitted means every
record is eligible; unselected records pass through unchanged. A
predicate error skips all enrichment without dropping telemetry.

For a resource or scope destination every predicate leaf must reference
that same table, so eligibility is uniform for its shared parent; a
record destination may reference any table. Selection is per record and
does not change output-collision rules.

AttributeLookupCast.description:
Supported key conversions. Doubles are excluded because the lookup indexes
do not accept floating-point keys; output columns may still contain them.

AttributeLookupInput.description: One exact attribute key supplying a probe input.

oneOf.description:
Explicit conversion before probing. Without a cast the input must
already match the table's key type. A conversion failure skips the
probe; composite keys are never implicitly stringified.

An `ip` key column or range point always needs `cast: ip`, because the
input arrives as a string and would otherwise miss every record. A
missing or contradicting cast is rejected when the table resolves.

key.description:
Dotted attribute key, matched byte for byte. A flattened array element
is addressed by its literal index, such as `interfaces.0.ifIndex`; no
segment carries a special meaning. Composite inputs align by parent ID,
never by Arrow row position.

oneOf.description:
Defaults to the rule's destination table. A record rule may also read a
resource attribute, resolved through the record's resource ID. No other
cross-table read is supported.

AttributeLookupMatch.description:
Bind attributes to the index already defined by the lookup table.

A hash table requires exactly its configured key columns and no `point`; a
range table its partition columns (possibly none) plus `point`. Bindings are
named, so YAML map order does not determine tuple order.

keys.description:
Lookup-table key/partition column -> input attribute. Empty only for an
unpartitioned range lookup. Range bound columns are not probe bindings.

oneOf.description:
Point to search for in a range index; absent for a hash lookup. An
explicit cast must be `integer` or `ip`, matching the table's range.

AttributeLookupRule.description: One indexed lookup and the attributes to populate from its matched row.

lookup_table.description: UUID of a configured lookup table. Names are not unique identifiers.

match.description: Input attributes supplying the table's hash key or partition/range key.

output.description:
Destination attribute key -> lookup-table column name. All columns come
from the same matched row, so extra outputs add no index probes. Values
keep their column types; IP values are emitted as strings.

table.description:
Destination attribute table and default location of input attributes.
`record` means log, span or metric attributes; it does not include metric
data-point attributes. All outputs belong to this table.

oneOf.description:
Further record-selection predicate, ANDed with the top-level `when`.
Omitted adds no restriction. A predicate error skips only this rule.

A record destination may reference record, resource or scope attributes;
a resource or scope destination only its own table — the same
restriction the inherited top-level predicate carries.

batch_size.description:
Omitted or 0 takes the default of 1000. At most 65535 on a listener or
monitor, which numbers a payload's rows with a `u16`; a sink only counts
whole payloads against it, so there it goes up to 2147483647.

batch_timeout.description: Milliseconds. Omitted or 0 takes the default of 1000.

Cef.description: CEF (Common Event Format), inside syslog or raw.

enabled.description:
Off, CEF records are plain syslog: no `cef` attribute, and their `rt`
and severity are not read. Raw CEF lines are still framed over TCP.

Cisco.description: Cisco IOS, IOS XR, NX-OS, ASA and FTD `%FACILITY-SEVERITY-MNEMONIC:` messages.

enabled.description:
Off, they are plain syslog: no `cisco` attribute, and the device's own
hostname, time and severity are not read.

Cise.description:
Cisco ISE / ACS parsing, and the reassembly of the events ISE splits into
segments.

enabled.description:
Off, ISE/ACS messages are plain syslog: one record per segment, no
`cise` attribute.

max_pending.description: Events held at once; past it the oldest is sent incomplete.

max_pending_bytes.description: Bytes held at once; past it the oldest event is sent incomplete.

max_segments.description:
Events split into more segments are not reassembled: each segment is
its own record. `1` turns reassembly off.

reassembly_timeout.description:
How long, in milliseconds, an event's first segment waits for the
rest before what arrived is sent as an incomplete event.

async_insert.description:
Server-side [async inserts]. Lets Clickhouse coalesce small INSERTs into
larger parts; keep it on unless `batch_size` is already >= a few thousand
rows per flush.

[async inserts]: https://clickhouse.com/docs/en/optimize/asynchronous-inserts

oneOf.description:
Run `CREATE DATABASE` / `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` on startup. Handy
for a first run; turn it off in production so workers don't race to
create tables and so schema changes stay under your control.

Omit the block to leave schema management entirely to you. The DDL knobs
inside it (`cluster_name`, `table_engine`, `ttl`) only apply at creation
time — changing them later does not alter existing tables.

enable_schema_validation.description: Enables schema validation at insert time at the cost of throughput

endpoints.description:
HTTP interface URLs, e.g. `http://ch-1:8123` or `https://ch-1:8443`.
Listing more than one turns on client-side routing (see `distribution`).
With chproxy/HAProxy or a `Distributed` table in front, list the single
front door and leave `distribution` at its default.

max_concurrent_inserts.description:
Inserts in flight to one endpoint at once, across the sink's workers.
A batch sends one insert per table, so this counts inserts, not
batches. Past it, a worker waits with its batch ready (the wait does
not count toward `write_timeout`). 0 (default) means no limit.

settings.description:
Extra Clickhouse session settings sent with every statement, e.g.
`max_execution_time: "60"`. Escape hatch for anything not modelled above.

wait_for_async_insert.description:
Block until an async insert is flushed to disk. Costs throughput, buys
durability. Ignored when `async_insert` is false.

ClickhouseCompression.description:
Wire compression for the HTTP interface. Mirrors what the Clickhouse Rust
client supports — gzip/deflate/br are not offered.

cluster_name.description:
Emits `ON CLUSTER <name>` in the generated DDL. Note this only spreads
the *DDL* across the cluster — it does not shard writes.

ttl.description:
Retention in seconds, applied as a `TTL` clause in the generated DDL.
0 disables it.

ClickhouseDistribution.description:
How batches are routed across `Clickhouse::endpoints`.

There is deliberately no `broadcast` (unlike [`OtelDistribution`]): sending
the same rows to every node would duplicate them, not replicate them.
Replication is Clickhouse's job — see `table_engine`.

ClickhouseTableEngine.description:
`ENGINE = <name>(<params>)` used when `create_schema` runs the DDL.
Combine with `cluster_name` and `ReplicatedMergeTree` for replication.

ClickhouseTables.description:
Destination table per signal. Metrics fan out by datapoint type because the
column layouts differ; this matches the OpenTelemetry collector's schema so
existing Grafana dashboards keep working.

host_ids.description: Hosts whose items the canvas may use.

inputs.description: List of processor IDs that are inputs to this sink.

channel_buffer_size.description:
Slots between the disk bridge and the consumer. A payload that finds a
free slot skips the disk; 0 spills whenever the consumer is busy.

max_disk_size.description:
Bytes of payloads (as stored, after compression) the topic holds
before a send waits or, with `non_blocking`, fails; 0 is unbounded.
Not the size of its files, which keep delivered payloads until a
compaction drops them.

transport_optimized.description:
Stores payloads in the OTAP transport encoding (batches sorted, ids
delta-encoded) before `compression`: smaller on disk, mostly for
metrics, for a costlier encode and decode. Payloads come back with
their attributes reordered. A topic still reads what it stored with
the other setting.

write_through.description:
Every payload is written to disk before it is handed on, and its key is
deleted only once the sink acks it, so a crash or kill loses nothing
that was accepted (at-least-once: expect duplicates after one). Only
for a sink's channel; `channel_buffer_size` then bounds what is read
ahead of the workers, not what skips the disk.

Failure.description:
`PartialEq` compares `at` by instant, not by rendered offset — that is what
`DateTime` equality means, and it is the right notion here: the wire form carries
an instant and no offset, so two failures that differ only in the zone they are
displayed in are the same failure.

last_updated.description: Send it back when saving the graph.
Send it back when saving the node's content.

oneOf.description: Null until a sink is chosen for the node.
Null until a sink is chosen for the node.
Null empties the node.
Null empties the node.

GraphNodeContentInput.description: The content of a node to save. Its kind must be the node's kind.

oneOf.description: Null until a sink is chosen for the node.
Null until a sink is chosen for the node.

processors.description: Every processor of the group, in execution order.

processor_id.description: A new id creates the processor, an id of this group updates it.

sink_id.description: Must be in the pipeline's sink subset.

total.description: All matching items, ignoring limit and offset.

add.description: Items to add. Items already in the source are skipped.

remove.description: Items to remove. Items not in the source are skipped.

name.description: The item's own name, or the name of the template item it comes from.

InternalLogsListener.description:
Exports patrolli's own logs as log records, one per event, with the event's
fields and its enclosing spans' fields as record attributes.

buffer_size.description:
Events held between capture and this listener; beyond it events are
dropped and counted, never waited for.

exclude.description:
Modules never exported. The longest matching prefix wins, so an entry
can carve a submodule out of an include.

include.description: Modules to export, each at its own level. Empty exports `patrolli` at `level`.

oneOf.description: Level for `patrolli` when `include` is empty.

InternalMetricsListener.description:
Reports this node's own internal metrics every `interval`. Every main node
runs its listeners, so each node reports itself under its own
`patrolli.node.id` scope.

interval.description:
Time between two reports. Snapshots refresh every
`global.internal_metrics_interval`, so a shorter interval repeats them.

report_throughput.description:
Log signal only: report per-second rates diffed against the previous
snapshot instead of raw cumulative values.

InternalMetricsSignal.description: Which OTel signal the `internal_metrics` listener emits.

ItemState.description:
Coarse health of an item, computed once on the write path so that every
reader (gRPC, REST, the Prometheus exporter) agrees without re-deriving it
from timestamps and cron schedules.

Discriminants match `v1::ItemState` one-for-one, so the conversion is a
cast. `Unknown` is 0 so a freshly zeroed `AtomicU8` is valid.

max_message_size.description:
Largest message the producer sends, in bytes (librdkafka's
`message.max.bytes`), checked before compression; a bigger one is
rejected without being sent. The broker checks its own
`max.message.bytes` against the compressed batch, so raising this lets a
compressible message past librdkafka for the broker to judge. 0 takes
librdkafka's default of 1000000.

producer_count.description:
How many librdkafka producers the sink's workers share, taken
round-robin per batch. Each worker has one batch in flight, so
`worker_count` is the write concurrency; this only sets how many clients
(each with its own queue, broker threads and connections) carry it.

write_timeout_seconds.description:
How long one attempt at a batch may take (`message.timeout.ms`); a
batch not delivered by then is retried per the sink's `retry:`.
0 takes the default of 30.

oneOf.description:
Match by endpoint source ip, only supported on endpoint defined with IP.
Hostname is not supported.

allOf.description:
The object name out of an OID as the MIB renders it,
`MODULE::object.instance`: `IF-MIB::ifDescr.33` -> `ifDescr`. Cheaper
than the equivalent regular expression.

oneOf.description:
The object name out of an OID as the MIB renders it,
`MODULE::object.instance`: `IF-MIB::ifDescr.33` -> `ifDescr`. Cheaper
than the equivalent regular expression.

allOf.description: One capture group of a regular expression, for names in any other shape.

oneOf.description: One capture group of a regular expression, for names in any other shape.

NameFormat.description:
Normalization applied to a pivot element's raw name before it is matched to
a column. A raw name that does not fit the format binds no column.

max_sources.description:
Exporter sources tracked for template state, per parser shard. The
parser is sharded by source IP, so the process-wide ceiling is this
times the shard count.

prune_idle_after.description: A source unseen for this long is dropped by the sweep.

prune_interval.description: How often idle sources are swept out of the parser caches.

end.description: index of the last sub-identifier to take, inclusive

start.description: index of the first sub-identifier to take, inclusive

owner_user_id.description: Null when the owner was deleted. Such a pipeline is always public.

PipelineGraph.description:
The structure of a canvas. What a node holds is edited per node; the graph
only carries a read-only summary of it.

PipelineGraphInput.description:
A graph to save. It has the shape GET returns, so a client can send back
what it read after editing it. The `data` of each node is ignored.

PipelineSubsetInUse.description: What still uses the hosts and sinks a request drops.

item_ids.description: The first items of dropped hosts, at most 100.

node_ids.description: Source nodes holding items of dropped hosts, and sink nodes of dropped sinks.

group.description:
Capture group whose text becomes the name, `0` being the whole match.
Must exist in `pattern`. An unmatched or empty group binds no column.
Defaults to `1`.

pattern.description:
Regular expression in Rust `regex` syntax, searched anywhere in the raw
name; the first match is used. Invalid syntax is rejected when the
config is read.

last_updated.description: Send it back when saving the graph.
Send it back when saving the node's content.

owner_user_id.description: Null when the owner was deleted. Such a pipeline is always public.

refresh_token.description: Unchanged by a refresh; reuse it until it expires.

data.description:
An applied template item inherits name, schedule, timeout_ms and config from
the template item it is derived from. Any of those fields that is provided
overrides the inherited value, and any field left null keeps inheriting.

A root template item owns its values, so name, schedule, timeout_ms and
config are mandatory. A template item linked from another template inherits
them, so they are optional there and only need to be set to override.

Retry.description:
How a sink paces the retries of a batch its destination could not take:
`initial_interval`, growing by `multiplier` up to `max_interval`.

initial_interval.description: Milliseconds before the first retry. Omitted or 0 takes the default of 1000.

max_elapsed.description:
Milliseconds a batch is retried for before it is dropped. 0 (the
default) retries until it lands.

max_interval.description:
Milliseconds; the longest wait between two retries. Omitted or 0 takes
the default of 60000.

multiplier.description:
Growth of the wait from one retry to the next, at least 1. Omitted or 0
takes the default of 2.

Sensitive.description: Write-only secret. Send the value as a string. Responses return {"set": "<handle>"}; send that object back unchanged in an update to keep the stored value.

SnmpObjectFormat.description:
Options of the `snmp_object` name format.

The `MODULE::` prefix, when present, is always dropped. A raw name without a
MIB match — a bare numeric OID such as `1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.2.33` — comes out
as its first arc (`1`) and so matches no column, which is the intent.

strip_instance.description:
Also drop the instance suffix after the object name: `ifDescr.33` ->
`ifDescr`, `sysName.0` -> `sysName`. With `false` the column is named
`ifDescr.33`. Defaults to `true`: for a table walked in `table_format`
the instance is already carried by the row's `snmp.id`.

max_unknown_oids_per_row.description:
How many of the configured OIDs may produce no value for a row before that
row is discarded instead of shipped incomplete.

Counts every OID in the config forest, chained ones included, so `0` demands
that every one of them resolve. Omitted (`null`) disables the check and every
row is emitted whatever it holds. Only meaningful with `table_format`, which
is the only mode that has rows.

StatsSnapshot.description:
One read of a [`Stats`], flattened for transport.

Cheap to produce: the failure fields are `Arc` clones, not deep copies, so a
snapshot of an item with a full ring costs two atomic increments.

Everything here is in its final consumable form, because a snapshot is read far
more often than it is produced and every consumer would otherwise repeat the
same conversions. Timestamps are `DateTime<FixedOffset>` carrying the offset the
caller passed to [`Stats::snapshot_at`] — the same shape and offset as
[`Failure::at`], so the fields are directly comparable — and the activity planes
are packed bytes with the stale tail already masked off. The atomics behind all
of this are still millis and words; that's a storage detail, not an interface.

activity_ok.description:
The trailing 24 hours as 288 five-minute buckets, ending at
`activity_window_end`. [`ACTIVITY_PLANE_BYTES`] each, LSB-first — bucket `i`
is bit `i % 8` of byte `i / 8` — or empty when the item recorded nothing in
the window.

Buckets address absolute time by tick modulo 288, so bucket 0 is always
00:00–00:05 UTC and every node agrees on what a position means; see
[`ActivityWindow`]. Buckets the item has not reached yet are already masked
off, so what is here is what is true.

A bucket set in neither plane had no result at all — a young item, a bucket
it wasn't due in, or one it went silent through. That is **not** a failure,
and for anything on a schedule slower than five minutes it is most buckets.

activity_window_end.description:
Start of the newest bucket in the window: the 5-minute boundary at or
before the read. The window covers the 288 buckets ending here, so bucket
`i` is the most recent tick `t <= end` with `t % 288 == i`.

last_attempt.description:
`None` where the event hasn't happened yet, so callers can tell "never
succeeded" from "succeeded at the epoch".

last_duration_ms.description:
`None` until the first check completes. A `Some(0)` record count is
meaningful: the check ran and returned nothing.

refresh_token.description: Unchanged by a refresh; reuse it until it expires.

oneOf.description:
An OPL program: the signals it applies to (`logs`, `traces`, `metrics`,
`signals`, or one metric type such as `gauges`) followed by
`|`-separated operators (`where`, `drop`, `set`, `rename`, `remove`,
`apply`, `if`/`else`), e.g.
`logs | where severity_number >= 17 | set attributes["critical"] = true`.

opl.description:
An OPL program: the signals it applies to (`logs`, `traces`, `metrics`,
`signals`, or one metric type such as `gauges`) followed by
`|`-separated operators (`where`, `drop`, `set`, `rename`, `remove`,
`apply`, `if`/`else`), e.g.
`logs | where severity_number >= 17 | set attributes["critical"] = true`.

Transform.description:
Transform telemetry with a program, keyed by its language (one key, e.g.
`opl: ...`). OPL is the only language so far.

Batches of a signal the program does not select pass through unchanged. A
batch the engine fails on is dropped and counted as errored. `route_to` is
not supported: route with processor inputs instead.

recv_buffer_size.description:
Kernel receive buffer (`SO_RCVBUF`) requested per socket, in bytes.
Granted in full with `CAP_NET_ADMIN`, otherwise capped at
`net.core.rmem_max`. The kernel doubles it for bookkeeping. 0 uses the
default (32 MiB).

spin_before_block_us.description:
Microseconds the reader keeps polling an empty socket before it
sleeps. Keeps the core out of deep idle states between back-to-back
datagrams, which only matters with a small `recv_buffer_size` and one
socket near 1M datagrams/s; every polled gap costs CPU, and a busy
socket pins a core. 0 (the default) sleeps as soon as the socket is
empty. At most 1000.

UpdateAppliedTemplateItemRequest.description:
An applied template item inherits name, schedule, timeout_ms and config from
the template item it is derived from. Any of those fields that is provided
overrides the inherited value, and any field left null keeps inheriting.

last_updated.description: The `last_updated` of the canvas when it was read.
The `last_updated` of the node when it was read.

force.description:
Take items of a dropped host off their sources and empty the sink
nodes of a dropped sink, instead of answering 409.

last_updated.description: The `last_updated` of the pipeline when it was read.

visibility.description: Only the owner can change it.

inputs.description:
List of processor IDs that are inputs to this sink.
If empty, the sink will have no inputs and will not receive any data.

UpdateTemplateItemRequest.description:
A root template item owns its values, so name, schedule, timeout_ms and
config are mandatory. A template item linked from another template inherits
them, so they are optional there and only need to be set to override.

UpdateUserRequest.description: Fields left out are kept as they are.
